transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-04 16:30 UTC | Duration: 58 min | Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tomás Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Olivia Park (Meridian CTO), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Marcus Hsu (Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Product), Speaker 1 (intern).

Auto summary (auto-generated): Kickoff for implementation enablement and sprint plan. Confirmed scope for pilot: ingest telemetry, run embeddings + reranker, initial private deployment in VPC, success metrics: 95th p50 latency, cost per 1M tokens under target, and weekly quality checks. Action items assigned: runbook, network diagram, access. Next steps: share runbook, schedule deep-dive architecture review.

Topics detected: onboarding runbook, VPC/on-prem considerations, data retention & SOC2, benchmark plan, rollout phases.

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Jared from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Priya our SE and Tomás, your CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Olivia: Doing good, Jared. Thanks, excited to get this moving.
[00:11] Lena: Hi all. We have a pretty packed agenda — want to make sure we sync on the sprint milestones and infra reqs.
[00:19] Priya: Quick note, I posted a short agenda and some links in the calendar invite — runbook draft, example benchmark sheet, and the private deploy checklist (link: https://app.redwood.ai/enablement/runbook).
[00:28] Marcus: Got it, I saw the link. We'll need to know exact firewall and peering reqs before we provision anything.
[00:33] Tomás: Totally — and we can jump into the VPC checklist later. Today I want to make sure we leave with a shared 2-week sprint plan for onboarding.

[00:45] Speaker 1: quick question about pricing — how does dedicated vs hosted...
[00:48] Jared: Yeah, we'll cover that briefly — but Tomás will follow up post-call with a short pricing note tailored to the pilot. For now, main focus is setup and success criteria.

[01:02] Lena: Our top constraints: data residency (EU), SOC2 requirements, and latency — specifically p95 under 600ms for our primary inference paths. Also minimal PII retention.
[01:12] Priya: Great constraints, we can map those to Redwood Private with EU region + KMS integration for keys; and we can recommend quantization and batching profiles to meet p95. There's always a tradeoff of throughput vs cost which we'll show in the benchmark sheet.

[01:30] Marcus: For the private deployment — is the control plane still hosted by Redwood or do we get a fully offline control plane? We need clarity for audit.
[01:36] Priya: Two options: 1) Private with customer-managed VPC where the control plane stays in Redwood managed region but the inference plane lives in your VPC; 2) On-prem packaged private deployment where the control plane is also customer-hosted — that's generally for air-gapped enterprises. For now, most pilots go with option 1.

[01:55] Olivia: For compliance team they'd prefer the on-prem packaged variant, but for kickoff we can start with the VPC model and evaluate.

[02:03] Jared: Ok noted — start with VPC/private inference in EU, escalate to on-prem if needed.

[02:12] Samir: Can we outline what success looks like for MVP? Our product goal is automated anomaly tagging in telemetry with a reranker. So success is quality of tags and latency. We also have a timeline: want pilot results within 6 weeks.

[02:24] Priya: Proposed MVP success criteria: 1) Integration: Redwood API receives sample telemetry and returns structured tags with >=0.78 precision on the test set; 2) Performance: p95 latency < 600ms and cost target (TBD); 3) Observability: logs and token-level cost breakdown available in console. We'll add a quality regression check weekly.

[02:46] Lena: The precision target 0.78 is fine but we need to capture false positives impact — is there easy rollback?
[02:51] Priya: Yes, we recommend canary rollouts with A/B policy + automatic fallback to a smaller model or cached responses if quality dips — the console supports that.

[03:05] Marcus: Network specifics — we use AWS EU-West-1, have strict egress rules, and we'll need SAML SSO for admin users. Also KMS: we use CloudHSM for keys.

[03:16] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS and can use SAML for SSO. For firewalls, we provide IP ranges and optional peering — I'll capture those in the runbook.

[03:28] Jared: Quick aside — competitors? Olivia had mentioned experimenting with Anthropic earlier. Any learnings?
[03:33] Olivia: We did a PoC with a hosted Anthropic flow and cost spiked on short sequences; also the latency was variable. We're interested in Redwood for predictable tail latencies and on-prem option.

[03:48] Priya: Understood. We'll include a benchmark comparing throughput/cost across quantization settings in the sheet.

[04:02] Tomás: Sprint plan proposal: Week 0 (this week) — access & auth, runbook review, dataset sample. Week 1 — private infra provisioning + small ingest. Week 2 — baseline benchmark and first model integration. Week 3 — quality tuning and canary. Week 4 — pilot review and next steps. Total: 4 weeks to initial pilot.

[04:25] Lena: That aligns with our 6-week goal with extra slack. Important: we need a gated sign-off from security after Week 1.

[04:32] Priya: We'll add a security gate checklist item: SOC2 scope doc, network diagram, KMS attestation.

[04:40] Marcus: On dataset sharing: we can't share PII. We'll provide synthetic telemetry and a labeled subset. Are there tools to run evals locally?

[04:48] Priya: Yes — we can provide an evaluation harness (small Python tool) that runs locally against a sandbox endpoint or offline eval runner. I'll attach the repo link in the runbook.

[04:59] Speaker 1: repo link?
[05:00] Priya: Yes, repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-eval (internal). We'll give read access.

[05:06] Jared: Let's walk through immediate action items — Tomás, can you confirm we have a single Slack channel + access to the console for Lena?
[05:12] Tomás: Yes, I'll create #meridian-redwood and add the core folks; Lena will get console admin role.

[05:18] Lena: Console admin is fine. Also want weekly office hours from SEs during the sprint.

[05:23] Priya: We'll block 2x 1-hour office hours per week for first two weeks.

[05:29] Jared: Great. Now quick technical deep-dive item — model selection and quantization. Priya, can you summarize recommended starting model for telemetry tagging?

[05:35] Priya: Start with a mid-size open model we’ve validated (we call it rwd-small-v2 in the catalog) with int8 quantization for cost/latency balance. If quality is insufficient, we scale to rwd-medium or try mixed-precision. We'll instrument KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated tokens cost.

[05:53] Marcus: Any known issues with our log shaping? Our sequences are sometimes long.
[05:56] Priya: We’ll use chunking and a sliding window to minimize sequence length exposure and use the runtime kernel selection for longer contexts. Also, we can recommend embedding + retrieval for long histories.

[06:08] Samir: For observability — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency. Is that in console?

[06:12] Tomás: Yes, console provides per-route breakdowns, trace hooks, and you can configure retention. We discussed extended retention as an add-on if you need long-term logging.

[06:22] Olivia: Security team will ask for audit logs and evidence of encryption at rest and in transit. Can you supply SOC2 artifacts?

[06:27] Jared: Absolutely — we'll share SOC2 type II report, encryption attestation, and the security questionnaire we completed for other customers. I'll throw those in the doc drop.

[06:35] Lena: Good. Also, how do we handle training data drift / quality regression detection?

[06:39] Priya: Redwood Optimize has a quality monitoring pipeline we can wire up — it runs prompt-set based evals and alerts on regressions. We'll include a recommended prompt set for your telemetry categories.

[06:50] Marcus: One more infra detail: do you require a specific GPU type to run the private pool? We might prefer A10 or A100 based on cost.

[06:58] Priya: We support both A10 and A100; the runbook will include recommended hardware by model and quantization. For pilots, A10 is often cost-effective; for highest throughput, A100.

[07:07] Jared: Okay we're at 40 minutes in — let's surface any blockers.

[07:11] Olivia: Blockers: security sign-off timing, legal review of DPA, and finalizing dataset sanitization. If those take longer than two weeks it'll push timeline.

[07:21] Tomás: On DPA + legal — we can route to our contracts team; I'll attach a templated DPA and suggest a 7-day turnaround if possible.

[07:30] Priya: For dataset sanitization, we can provide a checklist and small script to mask PII before ingest.

[07:36] Lena: Excellent.

[07:39] Samir: Quick note on metrics: we want an initial dashboard with precision/recall, latency (p50/p95), and cost per 1M tokens. Is the dashboard templated?

[07:47] Tomás: Yes we'll provide a templated dashboard view in the console and can export to your BI.

[07:53] Jared: Time for a short recap and next steps.

[07:57] Jared: Recap — start with private VPC deployment in EU, 4-week sprint to pilot with a 6-week slack window. Success criteria: precision >= 0.78 on label set, p95 < 600ms, token cost target to be defined. Action items: Priya to share runbook and eval harness by 2025-11-07; Marcus to share network diagram by 2025-11-10; Tomás to post kickoff deck and Slack channel by 2025-11-05. Security gate post-Week 1.

[08:25] Olivia: Sounds good. Please include the DPA and SOC2 in the doc drop.

[08:30] Jared: Will do — I'll attach the SOC2 and DPA template.

[08:35] Lena: One last thing — can we book the architecture deep-dive with our infra leads for week of 2025-11-17?

[08:39] Priya: Yep, I'll propose two time slots after the call.

[08:44] Jared: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the runbook and schedule invites.

[08:48] Olivia: Thank you.

[08:50] Jared: End meeting.

Notes: Some transcription artifacts: 'rwd' model name might be misheard as 'rewd', and 'KV cache' occasionally transcribed as 'K V cash' in earlier version of transcript. Links shared: runbook (https://app.redwood.ai/enablement/runbook), eval repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-eval).
